title: Calibrated, pangenome-aware mapping quality (learned MAPQ with per-stratum conformal calibration)
mechanism: Treat MAPQ as a probability forecast and learn P(misplaced | features) from tandem-simulated reads drawn from donor-specific haplotypes. Features: aligner scores (AS, XS, chain/seed scores, number of sub-optimal hits), seed repetitiveness, pair consistency, local SD/TR annotation and pangenome features (how many HPRC haplotypes contain a near-equal alternative placement). A Mondrian (per-stratum) conformal or isotonic step then forces reported MAPQ to match empirical error within each stratum (unique, SD, satellite, MHC).
closest_prior_evidence: Qtip predicts MAPQ from tandem-simulated reads and is compatible with popular aligners; Cline 2020 recalibration raised SNP recall by 5.2%, 3.1% and 1.5% in rice, tomato and pepper (misaligned reads were 0.16% of training reads; F1 0.76-0.82 for detecting them).
github: https://github.com/BenLangmead/qtip (latest release v1.6.2; last push 2019-10; 25 stars)
status_evidence: Qtip exists but has had no push since 2019-10; no learned-MAPQ option is documented in the current release notes checked (minimap2 v2.31, strobealign v0.20.0); GitHub search 'mapping quality prediction machine learning' returned no genomics tool.
expected_impact: Accuracy: fewer false-negative and false-positive calls in LCRs, MHC and SDs, where MAPQ thresholds currently discard or admit reads; negligible runtime cost (post-hoc per-read model).
data_compute: Simulated reads from HPRC release-2 NA19240 and HG01943 haplotypes; truth through haplotype-to-GRCh38 alignments (impg GRCh38 PAF, 6.53 GB); CPU-hours; <8 GB RAM for the model.
risks: Simulation-to-real shift (error profiles, GC bias); model tied to aligner version; truly ambiguous paralog reads cannot be rescued by calibration alone (see P2); strata need enough misplaced reads.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 HPRC r2 maternal and paternal assemblies (assemblies_release2_v1.0.index.csv) as donor genome; 30x 2x150 bp simulated reads (sequencing errors only) on SD-rich chr1, chr15, chr16, chr22, mapped to GRCh38 no-alt with bwa 0.7.19, minimap2 2.31 -ax sr and strobealign 0.20.0; transfer test trained on HG01943 simulations; real-data check on NA19240 NYGC 30x CRAM (ERR3989410; md5 e6d4b9e1e19d1f4d4f5de6a0d16d9c10).
litmus_metric: Expected calibration error (ECE) and Brier score per stratum (UCSC genomicSuperDups, MHC, unique); yield = fraction of reads with calibrated P(correct) >= 0.999; DeepVariant v1.10 SNV/indel F1 in SDs on the real CRAM against NA19240 assembly-derived truth.
litmus_baseline: Not measured in this track; native MAPQ of each aligner is the baseline.
litmus_target: SD-stratum ECE <= 50% of native; >= 5% more SD reads at calibrated P(correct) >= 0.999; SD recall +>= 1 percentage point with no precision loss.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if all targets hold on NA19240 with a model trained only on HG01943; fail if calibration does not transfer across samples or F1 does not improve.
impact_justification: MAPQ thresholds gate nearly every downstream caller and misplacement concentrates in clinically relevant LCRs.
feasibility_justification: Needs only simulation, existing aligners and a small tabular model; laptop scale.
novelty_justification: Learned MAPQ exists (Qtip, Cline 2020) but is unused; pangenome features and per-stratum guarantees are new.

title: Paralog-aware Bayesian read allocation and joint calling in low-copy repeats
mechanism: Instead of discarding MAPQ-0 reads, treat each read's copy of origin among paralogs as latent; estimate paralog-specific copy number and PSV allele states jointly by EM or MCMC across all copies (as transcript quantifiers do), and emit posterior-weighted pileups or multi-locus genotypes, using a paralog catalogue derived from HPRC2 assemblies.
closest_prior_evidence: ParascopyVC reached precision 0.997 and recall 0.807 in 167 LCRs on simulations and mean F1 0.947 versus 0.908 for the best other caller across seven genomes; Paraphase profiles 160 long SD regions encoding 316 genes from HiFi.
github: https://github.com/tprodanov/parascopy (latest release v1.19.0) | https://github.com/PacificBiosciences/paraphase (latest release v4.1.0)
status_evidence: Open-source tools exist but are not defaults in GATK/DeepVariant short-read pipelines; DRAGEN multi-region joint detection (MRJD) is proprietary; it is enabled in the 1kG TruPath BAM headers, and its BED lists 19 regions totalling 405 kb (measured here).
expected_impact: Accuracy in medically relevant duplicated genes (e.g., PMS2, SMN1/2, STRC) where short-read pipelines lose recall.
data_compute: NA19240, NA19238 and NA19239 NYGC 30x CRAM region slices (MRJD regions are 0.05% of the NA19240 CRAM, measured here); truth gene copies from NA19240 HPRC r2 and HGSVC3 assemblies.
risks: Copy-number errors propagate to genotypes; the catalogue misses rare structural haplotypes; trio checks are needed.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 trio NYGC 30x CRAMs; DRAGEN TruPath calls for NA19238 (1kG-ONT bucket) as a proprietary comparator; regions = 19 MRJD regions plus the ParascopyVC LCR set.
litmus_metric: Per-gene copy-number accuracy; PSV-aware SNV/indel F1 against assembly truth; Mendelian consistency.
litmus_baseline: bwa-mem + DeepVariant with MAPQ filtering; not measured here.
litmus_target: LCR F1 >= 0.95 and exact copy number for >= 95% of genes.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if the open method matches ParascopyVC's published mean F1 (0.947) on NA19240 and beats MAPQ-filtered DeepVariant recall by >= 5 points.
impact_justification: Directly recovers clinically important genes.
feasibility_justification: Tools and truth exist; target regions are tiny.
novelty_justification: Implemented, mostly not adopted.

title: Li-Stephens mosaic reference: haplotype-copying alignment against a population panel
mechanism: Model the sample as an imperfect mosaic of panel haplotypes (Li-Stephens HMM with switch penalty rho and mismatch penalty theta). Infer a diploid mosaic from read k-mers (as haplotype sampling or PHI do), then align reads to the inferred paths or chain with a per-switch recombination penalty (Minichain), and report MAPQ as a posterior over (locus, haplotype path); coordinates lift back to GRCh38/CHM13 through the graph.
closest_prior_evidence: Haplotype sampling imputes a personalized subgraph by sampling local haplotypes from read k-mer counts; Minichain adds a recombination penalty to sequence-to-graph alignment (O(|Q||E||H|)) and better matches true recombinations on 60 MHC haplotypes; Locityper reaches median QV > 35 across 256 medically relevant loci, 10.9 points above Illumina pipelines.
github: https://github.com/at-cg/minichain (latest release v1.3; last push 2024-05; 29 stars) | https://github.com/vgteam/vg (latest release v1.78.0) | https://github.com/tprodanov/locityper (latest release v1.8.1; last push 2026-11; 51 stars) | https://github.com/eblerjana/pangenie (latest release v4.2.2)
status_evidence: k-mer-based haplotype sampling ships in vg Giraffe (vg v1.78.0); a recombination-penalised alignment posterior exists only in Minichain (2024) and PHI (2024 preprint).
expected_impact: Accuracy and reduced reference bias in polymorphic SDs, MHC/KIR and SV-adjacent sequence; largest for genomes distant from GRCh38 (e.g., YRI).
data_compute: HPRC r2 MC GRCh38 GBZ (5.42 GB) and .hapl (21.42 GB); leave-trio-out panel (remove NA19238/NA19239/NA19240 haplotypes); NA19240 NYGC CRAM; full-graph Giraffe indexes are likely tight in 64 GB.
risks: Switch and mismatch penalties are sensitive (Li-Stephens solution surface); panel composition bias; circular evaluation if the sample's haplotypes stay in the panel.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 NYGC 30x CRAM (ERR3989410; md5 e6d4b9e1e19d1f4d4f5de6a0d16d9c10); HPRC r2 GBZ/hapl with the trio's haplotypes removed; truth = NA19240 trio-phased HPRC r2 assemblies versus GRCh38. Arms: (a) bwa-mem to GRCh38, (b) Giraffe + haplotype sampling (vg 1.78.0), (c) recombination-aware mosaic (Minichain-style chaining or a PHI-inferred diploid personal reference).
litmus_metric: REF-allele fraction at truth heterozygous SNVs (reference bias); MAPQ >= 20 yield in SD/MHC; DeepVariant SNV+indel F1 in SD/MHC.
litmus_target: (c) reduces |REF fraction - 0.5| by >= 50% versus (a) and raises SD/MHC F1 by >= 2 points versus (b).
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if (c) beats (b) with a bootstrap CI excluding zero; if (c) and (b) tie, haplotype sampling already captures the headroom.
impact_justification: Reference bias affects every non-European genome and every polymorphic SD.
feasibility_justification: Leave-trio-out panels and graph indexes are heavy on 64 GB.
novelty_justification: Full recombination-aware alignment exists only in prototypes.

title: Calibrated per-base confidence for assemblies (conformal QV tracks)
mechanism: Emit a per-base error probability for every assembled base (FASTQ-like QV track or bigWig) from features such as per-haplotype read support, k-mer multiplicity, allele-specific coverage, HMM-Flagger state posteriors and repeat context; calibrate with split or Mondrian conformal prediction against labelled errors from independent assemblies of the same sample, so that 'at least 99.9% of bases labelled Q30 are correct' holds per stratum.
closest_prior_evidence: HMM-Flagger detects synthetic misassemblies with F1 78.4% (HiFi) and 60.4% (ONT R10) and estimates HPRC error rates of 0.94% (release 1) and 0.38% (release 2).
github: https://github.com/mobinasri/flagger (latest release v1.2.1; last push 2026-11; 132 stars) | https://github.com/logsdon-lab/NucFlag (latest release v1.0.2; last push 2026-10; 29 stars) | https://github.com/JiaoLaboratory/CRAQ (last push 2025-12; 99 stars) | https://github.com/marbl/merqury (latest release v1.4.1)
status_evidence: Existing tools output a global QV (Merqury), region flags (Flagger, NucFlag, CRAQ, Inspector) or per-region HMM states (HMM-Flagger); PubMed 'conformal prediction' AND genomics/sequencing (2022-2026) returned 35 records whose top six concern epigenetic clocks and clinical classifiers, none assemblies; GitHub search found no assembly tool.
expected_impact: Assembly QC and downstream use: callers, liftover and clinical users can weight or mask bases; errata lists become calibrated tracks.
data_compute: Independent assembly pairs of the same sample: HG00097 (HPRC r2 versus 1kG-ONT NAPU and R10 hifiasm assemblies) and NA19240 (HPRC r2 versus HGSVC3); HiFi/ONT/Illumina reads for features; CPU.
risks: Labels from assembly disagreement are noisy (either assembly can be wrong); exchangeability fails across strata unless calibrated per stratum; per-base tracks are large (run-length encode).
litmus_dataset: HG00097 and NA19240 assembly pairs; calibrate on chr1-11, test on chr12-22 and X.
litmus_metric: Empirical error rate per predicted-QV bin and conformal miscoverage per stratum (unique, SD, satellite).
litmus_baseline: Merqury global QV and HMM-Flagger states; not measured here.
litmus_target: Miscoverage within +/-0.5 percentage points of nominal at the 99% and 99.9% levels in every stratum.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if the guarantee holds on held-out chromosomes and on the second sample without recalibration.
impact_justification: Makes assembly errors quantifiable per base for every downstream user.
feasibility_justification: Independent assembly pairs and reads are public.
novelty_justification: No calibrated per-base assembly confidence tool found.

title: Pangenome-consistency screening for assembly errors
mechanism: Use the other ~460 HPRC2 haplotypes as a prior: structures and alleles that no other panel haplotype shares are enriched for assembly errors. Enumerate singletons from all-versus-reference alignments (impg/wfmash PAFs) or multi-MUMs (Mumemto), then test only those loci with the sample's own reads (HMM-Flagger or NucFlag-style coverage tests).
closest_prior_evidence: Mumemto computes multi-MUMs across 320 human assemblies (960 GB) in 25.7 h with <800 GB RAM and reveals aberrant assemblies and scaffolds; HPRC2 contributes 460 haplotypes and halves structurally unreliable regions relative to HPRC1.
github: https://github.com/vikshiv/mumemto (last push 2026-11; 141 stars) | https://github.com/pangenome/impg (latest release v0.5.0) | https://github.com/waveygang/wfmash (latest release v0.24.2)
status_evidence: Mumemto visualizes aberrant assemblies and impg queries homologous intervals; no tool turns panel singletons into read-tested error calls.
expected_impact: Assembly QC: cheap triage of candidate errors before read-based tests; useful for HPRC2/HGSVC3 errata and flagged-assembly case studies (HG01943).
data_compute: impg GRCh38 PAF (6.53 GB; every release-2 haplotype versus GRCh38); NA19240 and HG01943 HiFi/ONT; CPU.
risks: True private variants (de novo, rare SVs) are also singletons; population structure affects singleton rates.
litmus_dataset: impg all-versus-GRCh38 PAF filtered to NA19240#1/#2 and HG01943#1/#2; HiFi and ONT reads realigned to each assembly.
litmus_metric: Fraction of HMM-Flagger-unreliable bases recovered by singleton screening; precision of read-unsupported singleton events >= 50 bp.
litmus_target: >= 80% of HMM-Flagger-unreliable bases found while testing <= 5% of the genome; precision >= 50%.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if both hold on NA19240 and HG01943.
impact_justification: Makes population-scale assembly QC cheap and targeted.
feasibility_justification: All inputs are public PAFs and reads.
novelty_justification: Only visual or indirect prototypes exist.

title: Cloud-native region-sliced reanalysis of 1kG hard regions
mechanism: Fetch only the CRAM/BAM slices overlapping hard regions (SDs, MHC, TRs, MRJD genes) plus mates through HTTP range requests (htslib or htsget; refget for references), re-map them with improved methods (P1, P2, ML1) and publish per-region deltas for all 3,202 samples instead of re-processing whole genomes.
closest_prior_evidence: The 3,202-sample 1kG cohort was re-processed in full with DRAGEN (Behera 2024).
github: https://github.com/umccr/htsget-rs (last push 2026-08; 59 stars) | https://github.com/ga4gh/htsget (last push 2022-11; 15 stars)
status_evidence: Infrastructure exists, but no published workflow that re-maps only hard-region slices of the 1kG CRAMs was found. Measured here from the .crai alone: merged SDs on the GRCh38 primary chromosomes (166.9 Mb, about 5.4% of the genome) occupy 2.735 GB = 18.15% of the 15.07 GB NA19240 CRAM (19.96% including alt, random and unplaced contigs); the 19 MRJD regions occupy 8 MB (0.05%).
expected_impact: Cost and reach: makes P1, P2 and ML1 applicable to the full 1kG cohort on modest hardware.
data_compute: NYGC 30x CRAMs (ftp.sra.ebi.ac.uk, located through the 1kGP sequence index); GRCh38_full_analysis_set_plus_decoy_hla.fa for decoding; laptop scale.
risks: Mates mapped outside target regions need a second fetch; reads mis-mapped far away (the reason for reanalysis) are missed unless unmapped, decoy and alt slices are also scanned.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 NYGC 30x CRAM (ERR3989410; md5 e6d4b9e1e19d1f4d4f5de6a0d16d9c10).
litmus_metric: Bytes transferred; one-thread wall time; completeness = fraction of reads that a full re-map places in target regions and the sliced workflow also retrieves (measured on chr22 with a full download).
litmus_baseline: Measured: 18.15% of CRAM bytes for SDs on the primary chromosomes (18.60% with 1 kb padding; 19.96% and 20.44% including alt and unplaced contigs); 0.05% for the MRJD regions.
litmus_target: >= 99% completeness at <= 25% of bytes (SDs + mates + unmapped).
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met on chr22.
impact_justification: Unlocks cohort-scale use of every other improvement.
feasibility_justification: Measured byte fractions show it is cheap; mate handling is the open part.
novelty_justification: No such workflow found.

title: Open-source proximity-aware short-read mapping for Illumina TruPath (constellation) data
mechanism: TruPath reads carry flow-cell proximity information (reads from neighbouring clusters likely derive from the same template). An open mapper would group reads by proximity and score placements jointly, as linked-read aligners did with barcodes, rescuing SD reads and phasing variants; today this runs only inside DRAGEN.
closest_prior_evidence: Illumina markets TruPath Genome as proximity mapped read technology (formerly constellation) analysed in DRAGEN (vendor page, not peer reviewed: https://www.illumina.com/products/by-brand/trupath.html); linked-read mapping (Long Ranger) and alignment-free molecule mapping (MoleMap 2026) are the open precedents.
github: none found (GitHub searches 'illumina constellation' and 'linked-read alignment barcode' returned 0)
status_evidence: The public 1kG TruPath release (43 sample folders in the 1kG-ONT bucket) holds DRAGEN 4.5.4 BAMs made with --enable-proximity true; in the first 3,000 HG00097 records every read carries a 4-integer li:B array plus pp/PS tags, 446 carry BX, 400 HP and 271 xq (measured here); the header does not document tag semantics.
expected_impact: Accuracy in SD genes and long-range phasing from short reads; an open implementation lets the community test vendor claims and reuse proximity in other mappers.
data_compute: TruPath BAMs (~184-196 GB each, region-sliceable via .bai) for 43 1kG samples including NA19238 and five HPRC r2 and 1kG-ONT samples (HG00097, HG00253, HG00320, HG01258, HG03583).
risks: Undocumented tag semantics (reverse-engineering risk); chemistry licensing; DRAGEN may already be near-optimal.
litmus_dataset: TruPath BAMs for HG00097, HG00253, HG00320, HG01258 and HG03583; truth from their HPRC r2 and 1kG-ONT assemblies; regions = 19 MRJD regions plus SD genes. Arms: (i) the same reads re-mapped without proximity (bwa-mem2/minimap2), (ii) DRAGEN proximity alignment as released, (iii) open prototype using li/BX tags.
litmus_metric: Fraction of reads placed on the correct paralog (read-to-assembly truth); SNV/indel F1; phase NG50.
litmus_baseline: (ii) minus (i) = vendor headroom; not measured here.
litmus_target: (iii) recovers >= 90% of the (ii) minus (i) gain.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met in >= 4 of 5 samples.
impact_justification: First open method for a new, public, 1kG-linked data type.
feasibility_justification: Tag semantics undocumented; BAMs large but sliceable.
novelty_justification: No open implementation found.

title: Learned anchor and chain scoring for long-read mapping in repeats
mechanism: Keep the chaining DP but learn its scoring: a gradient-boosted or small neural scorer over anchor-gap features, diagonal drift, seed multiplicity and PSV density, trained on simulated reads with known origin, replaces hand-set gap costs, max-skip and chain filters; optionally learn per-seed down-weighting of repetitive minimizers.
closest_prior_evidence: Nearest precedents learn seed orders (DeepMinimizer) or EM-train substitution/gap parameters (LAST-TRAIN); none learns the chain score.
github: https://github.com/Kingsford-Group/deepminimizer (last push 2021-12; 0 stars) | no learned-chaining repository found (GitHub search returned 0)
status_evidence: PubMed query (chain* AND machine/deep learning AND read mapping/alignment/long reads, 2018-2026) returned 0 records; GitHub repository search for learned chaining returned 0.
expected_impact: Accuracy: fewer wrong primary placements of HiFi/ONT reads in SDs and tandem repeats; possible speed gain by pruning hopeless chains early.
data_compute: PBSIM3/Badread simulations from NA19240 HPRC r2 haplotypes (minimap2 v2.31 adds paftools sim2bed and badread2fa for truth BEDs); CPU training.
risks: Generalization across chemistries and references; gains may be absorbed by better MAPQ calibration (ML1); integration into C chaining loops.
litmus_dataset: Simulated HiFi (Q30) and ONT R10 reads from NA19240 maternal and paternal HPRC r2 haplotypes (chr1, chr15, chr16, chr22); real NA19240 HiFi 35.2x for runtime.
litmus_metric: Fraction of reads with a wrong primary locus in the SD stratum; runtime per Gb.
litmus_baseline: minimap2 2.31 (-x map-hifi, -x lr:hq); not measured here.
litmus_target: >= 30% fewer wrong SD placements at <= 1.2x runtime.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if the target holds on HG01943 simulations with a model trained on NA19240; fail otherwise.
impact_justification: Gains are confined to repeats; minimap2 is already accurate in unique sequence.
feasibility_justification: Training data is simulable and the DP is unchanged.
novelty_justification: No learned chain scorer found in literature or on GitHub.

title: Haplotype-safe deep-learning read correction and polishing (over-correction audit)
mechanism: Deep correction (DeepConsensus for HiFi; HERRO and hifiasm (ONT) for simplex ONT) and DL polishing (DeepPolisher) are mainstream; the gap is safety at heterozygous and paralog-specific sites. Proposal: (i) a standing over-correction audit counting true heterozygous/PSV alleles erased by correction against trio-phased truth; (ii) haplotype-aware correction with an explicit objective (minimum error correction, as in HALE) rather than heuristics.
closest_prior_evidence: HERRO raises read accuracy up to 100-fold for diploid human genomes and, with Verkko, reconstructs up to 32 chromosomes T2T with NGA50 >= 100 Mb; hifiasm (ONT) reaches near-T2T assemblies from standard simplex reads at an order of magnitude less compute; DeepPolisher improved predicted QV by 3.4 (54% error reduction) on 180 HPRC assemblies.
github: https://github.com/google/deepconsensus (latest release v1.2.0; last push 2026-04; 264 stars) | https://github.com/lbcb-sci/herro (latest release v0.1.1; last push 2026-09; 268 stars) | https://github.com/chhylp123/hifiasm (latest release 0.25.0) | https://github.com/google/deeppolisher (latest release r0.1.0; last push 2025-03; 111 stars) | https://github.com/at-cg/HALE (named in the HALE abstract)
status_evidence: Verkko v2.3.2 release notes accept HERRO- or hifiasm-corrected ONT simplex reads; NA19240 HiFi in HPRC r2 is DeepConsensus v1.2 output (data table production field); MEC-based haplotype-aware correction (HALE) is a 2026 prototype.
expected_impact: Accuracy and completeness: fewer collapsed haplotypes and paralogs; earlier detection of correction artefacts that propagate into T2T assemblies.
data_compute: NA19240 HPRC r2 ONT R10.4.1 73.9x (38.0x from reads >= 100 kb) and HiFi 35.2x; trio-phased NA19240 assemblies plus HGSVC3 NA19240 assembly as independent truth; GPU optional.
risks: Circularity if truth assemblies were built from the same corrected reads (use HGSVC3 and parental Illumina k-mers); ONT correction compute.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 ONT R10.4.1 and HiFi reads (HPRC r2), chr1, chr15, chr16, chrX.
litmus_metric: hifieval-style residual error and over-correction rate (truth heterozygous or PSV alleles flipped per 10 kb), stratified by SD, satellite and homopolymer context.
litmus_baseline: dorado correct (HERRO) and hifiasm (ONT) internal correction; not measured here.
litmus_target: Over-correction <= 1 per 10 kb at heterozygous sites in SDs with residual error <= Q30.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if both correctors meet the target; otherwise report the headroom (excess erased alleles) that haplotype-aware correction must capture.
impact_justification: Correction errors propagate silently into T2T assemblies used as references.
feasibility_justification: Public reads and truth exist; ONT correction compute is moderate.
novelty_justification: Correction is mainstream; the audit and MEC formulation are incremental.

title: Run-length BWT (r-index, move structure) seeding against hundreds of haplotypes
mechanism: Index all panel haplotypes in a run-length compressed BWT (size grows with the number of BWT runs, not total length) and compute MEMs/SMEMs or matching statistics against the whole panel; use panel-wide exact matches to seed alignment or to flag reads whose best match is a non-reference haplotype.
closest_prior_evidence: ropebwt3 indexed 320 assembled human genomes in 65 h at <= 170 GB peak memory and finds MEMs and affine-gap alignments; Movi answers matching queries up to 30x faster than earlier tools; b-move extends bidirectionally up to 7x faster than the br-index.
github: https://github.com/lh3/ropebwt3 (latest release v3.10; last push 2026-08; 134 stars) | https://github.com/mohsenzakeri/Movi (latest release v2.0.0) | https://github.com/biointec/b-move (last push 2025-04; 7 stars) | https://github.com/oma219/spumoni (last push 2024-04; 59 stars)
status_evidence: ropebwt3 v3.10 (2025-11-26) finds MEMs and inexact alignments over hundreds of genomes; no mainstream short- or long-read pipeline seeds against a panel run-length BWT.
expected_impact: Completeness and bias: exact matches to any panel haplotype; reference-bias-free read triage; memory proportional to runs.
data_compute: HPRC r2 haplotypes for one chromosome (~460 copies) or a prebuilt index; whole-panel construction needs >= 170 GB RAM per the ropebwt3 report, beyond a 64 GB laptop.
risks: Construction cost; locate queries slower than an FM-index; coordinates must be lifted from haplotypes to a reference.
litmus_dataset: HPRC r2 chr20 haplotypes minus the NA19240 trio (ropebwt3 index); NA19240 NYGC 30x reads from chr20 (region slice).
litmus_metric: Fraction of reads with an end-to-end exact match in the panel versus GRCh38; REF-allele fraction at truth heterozygous SNVs after panel-informed placement.
litmus_target: >= 10 percentage points more end-to-end exact reads and >= 50% reduction in |REF fraction - 0.5| at <= 3x bwa-mem runtime.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if both targets hold on chr20.
impact_justification: Directly attacks reference bias with exact panel matches.
feasibility_justification: Index construction exceeds laptop RAM at full scale.
novelty_justification: Mature research tools exist; adoption is the gap.

title: Low-density k-mer sampling (mod-minimizer, open-closed mod-minimizer, GreedyMini) in mainstream mappers
mechanism: Replace random-order minimizers (density 2/(w+1)) with schemes that approach the 1/w lower bound while keeping the window guarantee; fewer anchors give smaller indexes and cheaper chaining at equal sensitivity.
closest_prior_work: Groot Koerkamp 2024 [preprint] (10.1101/2024.05.25.595898); Groot Koerkamp 2025 (10.1186/s13015-025-00270-0); Golan 2025 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btaf251); Ndiaye 2024 (10.1186/s13059-024-03414-4); Frith 2023 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btad057); Li 2018 (10.1093/bioinformatics/bty191)
closest_prior_evidence: The mod-minimizer reduced index space by 15% for GRCh38 at (w,k) = (11,21) while keeping query time.
github: https://github.com/RagnarGrootKoerkamp/minimizers (last push 2026-07; 29 stars) | GreedyMini repository not found by GitHub search
status_evidence: Schemes are published with code; minimap2 v2.31 release notes list no change to k-mer sampling.
expected_impact: Memory and speed: smaller indexes and fewer anchors per read.
data_compute: GRCh38/CHM13 and NA19240 reads; CPU only.
risks: Gains shrink for small k; interaction with repeat masking; index format changes.
litmus_dataset: GRCh38 and CHM13 indexes; HiFi and Illumina reads simulated from NA19240 HPRC r2 haplotypes.
litmus_metric: Index size, anchors per read, chaining time, mapping accuracy.
litmus_target: >= 10% smaller index or >= 10% faster mapping with no accuracy loss.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met at matched (w,k) or matched density.
impact_justification: Broad but moderate resource savings.
feasibility_justification: A drop-in change to the sketching function.
novelty_justification: Published and coded but not adopted.

title: Exact second-pass alignment and optimality audit (A*PA2, BiWFA) for reads in repeats
mechanism: Run a fast exact aligner between the endpoints chosen by the heuristic mapper (banded extension with z-drop) and flag or replace alignments whose exact score differs; restrict to reads overlapping tandem repeats, SV breakpoints or low-identity stretches, where heuristics are most likely suboptimal.
closest_prior_work: Groot Koerkamp 2024 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btae032); Groot Koerkamp 2024 (10.4230/LIPIcs.WABI.2024.17); Groot Koerkamp 2024 [preprint] (10.1101/2024.03.24.586481); Marco-Sola 2020 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btaa777); Marco-Sola 2023 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btad074); Liu 2023 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btad487); Šošić 2017 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btw753); Suzuki 2018 (10.1186/s12859-018-2014-8); Aguado-Puig 2023 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btad701)
closest_prior_evidence: A*PA scales near-linearly at 4% divergence, is >500x faster than Edlib and BiWFA at n = 10^7 and d = 4%, and gives a 3x median speedup on long ONT reads.
github: https://github.com/RagnarGrootKoerkamp/astar-pairwise-aligner (no tagged release; last push 2026-05; 152 stars) | https://github.com/Marco-Sola-Lab/WFA2-lib (last push 2026-10; 232 stars)
status_evidence: A*PA/A*PA2 and BiWFA are released libraries; minimap2 performs heuristic banded extension (Li 2018) and its v2.31 notes list no change; wfmash uses WFA for base-level pangenome alignment (README).
expected_impact: Accuracy of indel/SV breakpoints and TR allele lengths; quantifies how often heuristics are suboptimal.
data_compute: NA19240 HiFi reads overlapping TR catalogues; CPU.
risks: A*PA/A*PA2 optimize unit-cost edit distance while mappers use affine gaps (use BiWFA for affine re-scoring); an optimal alignment can still be biologically wrong in repeats.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 HiFi 35.2x reads overlapping GRCh38 tandem repeats (region slice of minimap2 alignments).
litmus_metric: Fraction of alignments whose exact affine score exceeds the minimap2 score; TR allele-length concordance with NA19240 assembly truth.
litmus_target: Headroom test: adopt if >= 1% of TR reads change and TR concordance improves >= 1 point.
litmus_pass_fail: Fail (deprioritize) if < 0.1% of TR reads change.
impact_justification: Matters at TRs and breakpoints, not genome-wide.
feasibility_justification: Libraries exist; the audit is a short script.
novelty_justification: Implemented, not adopted as a second pass.

title: FracMinHash containment for population-scale assembly QC
mechanism: Estimate containment of read k-mers in assemblies (completeness) and of assembly k-mers in reads (spurious sequence) from scaled MinHash sketches with confidence intervals, instead of full k-mer databases.
closest_prior_evidence: FracMinHash containment comes with analytical confidence intervals (Hera 2023).
github: https://github.com/sourmash-bio/sourmash (latest release v4.9.4; last push 2026-11; 565 stars) | https://github.com/bluenote-1577/sylph (latest release latest) | https://github.com/bluenote-1577/skani (latest release latest)
status_evidence: Mature in metagenomics (sourmash v4.9.4); human assembly QC still uses full k-mer databases (Merqury).
expected_impact: Speed: completeness and contamination triage across hundreds of assemblies (1kG-ONT 500).
data_compute: Assemblies and Illumina reads for the 12 HPRC r2 and 1kG-ONT overlap samples.
risks: Sketches miss small, localized errors; complements rather than replaces Merqury.
litmus_dataset: The 12 samples with both HPRC r2 and 1kG-ONT assemblies plus NYGC Illumina reads.
litmus_metric: FracMinHash containment (k = 31, scaled = 1000) versus Merqury completeness; CPU time.
litmus_target: |difference| <= 0.5 percentage points with >= 50x less CPU; same ranking of the two assemblies per sample.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met for >= 11 of 12 samples.
impact_justification: Speeds cohort-scale QC.
feasibility_justification: Released tools; small inputs.
novelty_justification: Not used for human assembly QC.

title: Haplotype-aware graph indexes (GBWT/GBZ) with Giraffe for short and long reads
mechanism: Store haplotype paths through a pangenome graph in a GBWT and map reads with minimizer seeding constrained to observed haplotypes (Giraffe); recent work extends Giraffe to long reads and couples it to pangenome-aware DeepVariant.
closest_prior_evidence: Giraffe maps short and long reads to a >450-haplotype HPRC pangenome at speeds comparable to linear mappers and >10x faster than GraphAligner (2025 preprint); pangenome-aware DeepVariant reduces errors by up to 25.5%.
github: https://github.com/vgteam/vg (latest release v1.78.0) | https://github.com/jltsiren/gbwt (latest release v1.6) | https://github.com/google/deepvariant (docs include pangenome-aware WGS BWA/vg and WES case studies)
status_evidence: vg v1.78.0 (2026-10-19) ships Giraffe; google/deepvariant docs include pangenome-aware case studies.
expected_impact: Accuracy for short and long reads at near-linear-mapper speed; remaining gaps are adoption and laptop-scale memory.
data_compute: HPRC r2 MC GRCh38 GBZ (5.42 GB) + .hapl (21.42 GB); NA19240 reads.
risks: Index memory; graph coordinate conventions; leakage when the sample is in the graph.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 NYGC 30x CRAM (ERR3989410; md5 e6d4b9e1e19d1f4d4f5de6a0d16d9c10) and HPRC r2 NA19240 HiFi; HPRC r2 GBZ with the NA19240 trio removed.
litmus_metric: SNV/indel F1 against assembly truth; peak RSS and wall time on a 64 GB arm64 host.
litmus_target: F1 gain >= 1 point in SD/MHC strata at peak RSS <= 64 GB.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if both hold.
impact_justification: Large accuracy gains are already demonstrated.
feasibility_justification: Public graphs and indexes; memory is the main constraint.
novelty_justification: Mainstream; serves as the baseline for P1 and DS1.

title: Indel-robust and multi-length seeds (randstrobes, multi-context seeds, SubseqHash)
mechanism: Link k-mers across gaps (strobemers/randstrobes), store seeds of several lengths in one index (multi-context seeds) or hash ordered subsequences (SubseqHash) so seeds survive indels and nearby SNVs.
closest_prior_evidence: Multi-context seeds in strobealign improved accuracy over the previous version with little runtime cost and no memory overhead.
github: https://github.com/ksahlin/strobealign (latest release v0.20.0; last push 2026-11; 213 stars) | https://github.com/Shao-Group/SubseqHash2 (last push 2025-04; 8 stars) | https://github.com/Shao-Group/subseqhash3 (last push 2026-11; 0 stars)
status_evidence: strobealign is at v0.20.0 (2026-11-06) and implements multi-context seeds (Genome Biology 2026); SubseqHash2/3 remain research code.
expected_impact: Speed and indel sensitivity for short reads; SubseqHash targets error-prone long reads.
data_compute: Simulated reads from NA19240 haplotypes; NA19240 NYGC reads.
risks: Seed design interacts with repeat filtering; gains vary with read length.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 NYGC 30x CRAM (ERR3989410; md5 e6d4b9e1e19d1f4d4f5de6a0d16d9c10) and 2x150 simulations from NA19240 haplotypes.
litmus_metric: Mapping accuracy in indel-rich and SD strata; DeepVariant indel F1; throughput.
litmus_baseline: bwa 0.7.19 and minimap2 2.31 -ax sr; not measured.
litmus_target: Equal or better indel F1 at >= 2x throughput.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met.
impact_justification: Throughput and indel gains for the largest data type.
feasibility_justification: Released tool.
novelty_justification: Already released in strobealign.

title: Exact co-linear chaining with gap costs and overlaps (linear and graph references)
mechanism: Solve chaining exactly with gap costs and anchor overlaps (ChainX-style) or on DAG/pangenome graphs with gap-sensitive and haplotype-aware formulations, instead of heuristic max-skip/bandwidth chaining.
closest_prior_evidence: Graph-chaining formulations with gap costs were published in 2023-2024 with research implementations.
github: https://github.com/at-cg/minichain (latest release v1.3; last push 2024-05; 29 stars) | ChainX repository not found by GitHub search
status_evidence: Graph chaining is implemented in research tools (Minichain v1.3); linear mappers keep heuristic chaining.
expected_impact: Accuracy for long reads in SDs and large indels; mainly a correctness guarantee for chaining.
data_compute: Simulated ONT/HiFi reads from NA19240 haplotypes.
risks: Exact chaining is slow on repeats with many anchors; gains may be small after heuristics.
litmus_dataset: ONT R10 and HiFi simulations from NA19240 haplotypes (chr1, chr15, chr16, chr22).
litmus_metric: Fraction of reads whose heuristic chain differs from the optimal chain under the same score; change in mapping accuracy.
litmus_target: Headroom test: adopt if >= 0.5% of SD reads gain the correct placement.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met at <= 1.5x runtime.
impact_justification: Correctness gain concentrated in repeats.
feasibility_justification: Research code exists; simulation truth is easy.
novelty_justification: Prototype and published algorithms.

title: Methylation-aware phasing and haplotype tagging
mechanism: Use allele-specific methylation (5mC from ONT or HiFi kinetics) as extra haplotype-informative markers to bridge SNV-poor stretches in read-based and assembly-graph phasing.
closest_prior_evidence: MethPhaser lengthened phase N50 by 78-151% on ONT R9/R10 cell-line data at 83.4-98.7% phasing accuracy.
github: https://github.com/treangenlab/methphaser (last push 2025-03; 58 stars)
status_evidence: MethPhaser is released (2024) but is not part of the HPRC/HGSVC phasing defaults reviewed here.
expected_impact: Phasing completeness in long homozygous stretches.
data_compute: HPRC r2 hifi_meth_wg (232 samples; NA19240 at 41.8x) and ONT R10 with 5mC tags (the 1kG-ONT R10_HIFIASM folder lists dorado 5mCG_5hmCG basecalls for HG00097).
risks: Methylation is tissue- and cell-line-specific; X inactivation and imprinting violate assumptions.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 HPRC r2 HiFi with methylation (hifi_meth_wg) and trio-phased assemblies.
litmus_metric: Phase-block NG50 and switch error against trio truth.
litmus_target: >= 50% longer NG50 at <= 1.2x switch error.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met.
impact_justification: Useful where trios and Hi-C are absent.
feasibility_justification: Data and tool are public.
novelty_justification: Implemented, not adopted.

title: Signal-space mapping and assembly of ONT reads (pod5)
mechanism: Map or overlap raw current signals directly (hash-based quantized events, signal-space chaining, r-index classification), or feed current-level models into base-space alignment to rescue alignments near SVs; use signal where basecalls are ambiguous.
closest_prior_work: Kovaka 2020 (10.1038/s41587-020-0731-9); Zhang 2021 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btab264); Firtina 2023 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btad272); Firtina 2024 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btae478); Shivakumar 2024 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btae213); Firtina 2026 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btag087); Joshi 2023 (10.1093/bioinformatics/btad580); Mao 2022 (10.1109/micro56248.2022.00056); He 2025 (10.1038/s43588-025-00867-w)
closest_prior_evidence: RawHash2 improves F1 by 10.57% on average and throughput 4.0x over RawHash; Rawsamble overlaps raw signals with 5.01x average speedup and 5.74x lower peak memory than basecall-then-overlap; HQAlign finds 4-6% complementary SVs and raises the CHM13 alignment rate from 85.64% to 89.35%.
github: https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/RawHash (latest release v2.1; last push 2026-01; 71 stars) | https://github.com/skovaka/UNCALLED (last push 2024-03; 531 stars) | https://github.com/vikshiv/sigmoni (last push 2024-08; 7 stars)
status_evidence: Used for adaptive sampling and research benchmarks; no production human pipeline aligns or assembles in signal space.
expected_impact: Speed (triage without basecalling) and possibly accuracy near SVs; uncertain for paralogs.
data_compute: 1kG-ONT pod5 R10 for HG00097, HG00253, HG00320, HG01258, HG03583 and GM19238 (prefixes verified here); HPRC r2 assemblies of the same samples as truth.
risks: Signal models are chemistry-specific; basecaller progress may erase the gain.
litmus_dataset: HG00097 R10 pod5 subset (reads whose basecalls map to GRCh38 SDs); HG00097 HPRC r2 assembly as truth.
litmus_metric: Mapping concordance with dorado + minimap2; accuracy against read-to-assembly truth; time per read on Apple silicon.
litmus_target: >= 95% concordance at >= 2x lower compute, or higher accuracy in SDs.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if either holds.
impact_justification: Speed for triage; accuracy gains unproven.
feasibility_justification: Public pod5 for 1kG samples, but signal data are large.
novelty_justification: Prototype outside adaptive sampling.

title: Apple-silicon, ARM and GPU kernels for chaining and extension
mechanism: Port the two hot loops (chaining DP and banded extension) to GPU (CUDA, ROCm, Metal) or wide SIMD (NEON, SVE), exploiting unified memory on Apple silicon so indexes need no host-device copies.
closest_prior_evidence: Chaining takes 40-68% of minimap2 time for long reads, and mm2-gb reports 2.57-5.33x speedups on an AMD MI210; a BWA-MEM2 port to A64FX gave 11.6% better energy-to-solution than Skylake at lower performance.
github: https://github.com/Marco-Sola-Lab/WFA-GPU (last push 2026-11; 42 stars) | https://github.com/nanoporetech/dorado (README: runs on Apple silicon with Metal optimisations for inference) | no Metal alignment kernel found (GitHub search returned 0)
status_evidence: minimap2's README documents NEON builds; the bwa-mem2 README mentions no ARM build; dorado documents Metal optimisations for neural-network inference only; CUDA/ROCm mappers are prototypes.
expected_impact: Speed and energy on laptops and ARM servers; enables local reanalysis.
data_compute: NA19240 HiFi/ONT subsets; Apple M-series GPU.
risks: Small Metal bioinformatics ecosystem; numerical determinism; maintenance across GPU vendors.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 ONT R10 reads for chr20 (region slice).
litmus_metric: Reads/s and joules per Gb with byte-identical PAF versus the minimap2 2.31 NEON build.
litmus_baseline: minimap2 2.31 on an M1-class CPU; not measured here.
litmus_target: >= 2x throughput with identical output.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met.
impact_justification: Speed and energy, not accuracy.
feasibility_justification: GPU kernel engineering is substantial.
novelty_justification: Metal alignment kernels not found.

title: Minimizer-space graphs for assembly and mapping
mechanism: Operate on sequences of minimizers instead of bases (minimizer-space de Bruijn graphs, MBG, multiplex dBG) to compress repeats and speed assembly; map accurate long reads in minimizer space (mapquik).
closest_prior_evidence: Verkko builds on MBG; metaMDBG and nanoMDBG are published minimizer-space assemblers.
github: https://github.com/ekimb/mapquik (no tagged release; last push 2023-10; 70 stars) | https://github.com/ekimb/rust-mdbg (latest release v1.0.1; last push 2024-09; 181 stars) | https://github.com/maickrau/MBG (latest release v1.0.17)
status_evidence: Mainstream in assembly (Verkko/MBG, metaMDBG); mapping in minimizer space remains a prototype (mapquik has no tagged release and no push since 2023-10).
expected_impact: Speed for HiFi mapping; assembly already benefits.
data_compute: NA19240 HiFi 35.2x.
risks: Sensitivity loss for noisier reads; base-level alignment still needed.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 HiFi reads (chr20 region slice) and HiFi simulated from NA19240 haplotypes.
litmus_metric: Mapping accuracy (simulated truth); throughput.
litmus_target: >= 5x throughput at <= 0.1 percentage point accuracy loss.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met.
impact_justification: Throughput gains for accurate long reads.
feasibility_justification: Released code; simulation truth is easy.
novelty_justification: Mainstream for assembly; mapping is a stale prototype.

title: Proximity ligation (Hi-C, Pore-C, CiFi) for phasing and scaffolding
mechanism: Use chromatin contacts to phase haplotype graphs and scaffold contigs; long-read variants (Pore-C, CiFi) give multi-contact, variant-rich reads.
closest_prior_evidence: Verkko2 assembles an average of 39 of 46 complete chromosomes as scaffolds on 19 genomes, 21 as gapless contigs.
github: https://github.com/c-zhou/yahs (latest release v1.2.2; last push 2024-11; 186 stars) | https://github.com/zengxiaofei/HapHiC (last push 2026-08; 288 stars) | https://github.com/marbl/verkko (latest release v2.3.2)
status_evidence: Hi-C phasing is built into hifiasm and Verkko2; HPRC r2 lists Hi-C for 225 samples.
expected_impact: Phasing and scaffolding for non-trio samples.
data_compute: HG00097 Hi-C 174.8x and HG01943 Hi-C 124.8x (HPRC r2).
risks: Incremental; Hi-C misjoins in SDs.
litmus_dataset: HG01943 HiFi 67x + ONT 62.6x + Hi-C 124.8x (HPRC r2).
litmus_metric: Switch and Hamming error and chromosome-scale phasing against the HPRC r2 assembly (and parental k-mers if available).
litmus_target: Verkko2 Hi-C mode with equal or lower switch error.
litmus_pass_fail: Report the better mode; no novelty claim.
impact_justification: Matters for non-trio samples.
feasibility_justification: Data and tools are public.
novelty_justification: Mainstream.

title: Graph neural networks for residual assembly-graph tangles
mechanism: Train a GNN on assembly graphs whose true paths are known (simulated or from T2T assemblies) to score edges and paths; apply it only to residual tangles (rDNA, large SDs, acrocentric arms) left unresolved by hifiasm/Verkko, abstaining when confidence is low.
closest_prior_evidence: GNNome reconstructs HiFi assemblies with contiguity and quality comparable to state-of-the-art tools across several species.
github: https://github.com/lbcb-sci/GNNome (latest release 0.4.0; last push 2025-12; 52 stars) | https://github.com/lbcb-sci/DipGNNome (last push 2025-09; 4 stars; diploid variant; no paper found)
status_evidence: GNNome is published and released (0.4.0); a diploid repository exists without a paper; no production assembler uses GNN path selection.
expected_impact: Completeness in the hardest loci; HPRC2 already reports thousands of T2T chromosomes, so headroom is concentrated in few regions.
data_compute: HiFi + UL ONT graphs (hifiasm 0.25.0, Verkko 2.3.2); training labels from HPRC2/HGSVC3 T2T contigs; GPU or Apple MPS.
risks: Label leakage when training and testing on HPRC samples; opaque failures; diploid and UL graphs differ from training graphs.
litmus_dataset: HG00097 (HPRC r2 HiFi 63.7x, ONT R10 57.1x, Hi-C 174.8x) and NA19240; residual tangles = graph components overlapping gaps or HMM-Flagger-unreliable blocks in HPRC r2 assemblies.
litmus_metric: Fraction of residual tangles resolved; misjoins against the independent 1kG-ONT assembly (HG00097) or HGSVC3 (NA19240).
litmus_baseline: hifiasm 0.25.0 and Verkko 2.3.2 graphs; not measured here.
litmus_target: >= 25% of residual tangles resolved with zero new misjoins.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met on both samples with a model not trained on either sample.
impact_justification: Remaining tangles are few but biologically important.
feasibility_justification: Needs GPU training and diploid graph handling.
novelty_justification: Published prototype; absent from production assemblers.

title: Strand-seq for phasing and orientation QC of assemblies
mechanism: Single-cell template-strand sequencing gives chromosome-length phasing and strand orientation; use it to phase assembly graphs (Graphasing) and to detect misoriented contigs and inversions.
closest_prior_work: Human Genome Structural Variation Consortium 2020 (10.1038/s41587-020-0719-5); Henglin 2024 (10.1186/s13059-024-03409-1)
closest_prior_evidence: Graphasing phases assembly graphs comparably to trio phasing, beats Hi-C in phasing accuracy and yields >18 chromosome-spanning haplotypes.
github: https://github.com/ptrebert/project-diploid-assembly (PGAS workflow)
status_evidence: Graphasing is published (Genome Biology 2024); Strand-seq is unavailable for most 1kG samples.
expected_impact: Phasing completeness and inversion QC where trios and Hi-C are absent.
data_compute: HGSVC Strand-seq libraries; availability for NA19240 not verified in this scan.
risks: Data scarcity; library QC.
litmus_dataset: HGSVC Strand-seq for NA19240 (to verify) and NA19240 HPRC r2 assemblies.
litmus_metric: Misoriented segments and inversion concordance with HGSVC3 calls.
litmus_target: All misorientations >= 10 kb detected.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if Strand-seq orientation agrees with HGSVC3 inversions.
impact_justification: Orientation errors are rare but consequential.
feasibility_justification: Data access to verify.
novelty_justification: Implemented in consortium pipelines.

title: Genomic language models as sequence priors for correction, polishing and mapping
mechanism: Use a pretrained DNA language model's likelihoods or embeddings as a prior over local sequence (low-coverage polishing or correction) or as read embeddings for candidate search.
closest_prior_evidence: Nucleotide Transformer was trained on 3,202 human genomes plus 850 other species; Feng 2025 found general DNA foundation models less effective than specialized models for expression and causal-QTL tasks while competitive for pathogenic-variant identification.
github: https://github.com/ArcInstitute/evo2 (latest release v0.5.0) | https://github.com/kuleshov-group/caduceus (latest release v0.1.0; last push 2026-03; 254 stars) | https://github.com/instadeepai/nucleotide-transformer (no tagged release; last push 2026-11; 942 stars)
status_evidence: Alignment and correction uses exist only as preprints (Embed-Search-Align 2023; LLMED 2025); no production aligner or assembler uses a gLM prior.
expected_impact: Uncertain and possibly negative for accuracy: a prior learned from reference-like sequence pulls calls toward common alleles.
data_compute: GPU inference; NA19240 reads and assemblies.
risks: Systematic bias against rare and de novo alleles; training-set leakage (Nucleotide Transformer saw the 3,202 1kG genomes, so 1kG litmus samples are in-distribution); per-base compute cost.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 HiFi downsampled to 5x and 10x; truth = trio-phased NA19240 assemblies; NA19240-private alleles (absent from the other 3,201 1kGP high-coverage samples).
litmus_metric: Consensus QV; rare-allele erasure rate (private alleles converted to the reference or a common allele).
litmus_baseline: Pileup or DeepPolisher consensus without a prior; not measured here.
litmus_target: QV gain >= 1 at 5x with erasure increase <= 0.1 percentage point, using a model whose training data excludes the 1kGP samples.
litmus_pass_fail: Fail if erasure rises above target or if gains appear only with a 1kG-trained model.
impact_justification: Benchmarks show weak zero-shot value, and the bias risk is direct.
feasibility_justification: Models are public but GPU-heavy.
novelty_justification: Absent from production aligners and assemblers.

title: Learned edit-distance embeddings and locality-sensitive bucketing for candidate generation
mechanism: Map reads or windows into a vector space whose distance approximates edit distance (CGK, tensor sketch, NeuroSEED, LSB/MELO-ED, LOCALE) and retrieve candidates by nearest-neighbour search instead of exact seed hits; aimed at divergent or noisy sequence.
closest_prior_evidence: LOCALE retains 63.2% recall at 10% variation on a 50-accession SRA benchmark where k-mer indexes and earlier DNA embeddings fall below 35%.
github: https://github.com/gcorso/NeuroSEED (no tagged release; last push 2023-10; 76 stars) | https://github.com/ratschlab/tensor-sketch-alignment (last push 2022-11; 13 stars)
status_evidence: All are research code or preprints; no human read mapper seeds with learned embeddings.
expected_impact: Sensitivity for divergent sequence (SV alleles, divergent haplotypes, raw signal); limited for routine human mapping.
data_compute: CPU/GPU embedding inference; NA19240 ONT reads.
risks: Approximation error; size of dense-vector indexes; speed relative to minimizers.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 ONT R10 reads overlapping GRCh38 SDs and divergent HLA/KIR loci (region slice).
litmus_metric: Recall of the true locus among top-k candidates at matched candidate count; wall time.
litmus_target: >= minimap2 recall at <= 2x time in divergent loci.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met.
impact_justification: Human mapping is already well served by minimizers.
feasibility_justification: Code exists; integration is research work.
novelty_justification: Not used for human read mapping.

title: Differentiable dynamic programming to learn platform-specific alignment scoring
mechanism: Relax the max in Smith-Waterman to a smooth operator so alignment becomes differentiable, then fit substitution, gap and context-dependent (homopolymer) parameters end to end against truth alignments for each chemistry (ONT R10, Element, Ultima, Roche SBX).
closest_prior_evidence: Differentiable alignment is established for protein MSAs and embeddings; LAST-TRAIN fits DNA scoring parameters by EM.
github: https://github.com/avitai/DiffBio (2 stars; last push 2026-11) | SMURF repository not found by GitHub search
status_evidence: For DNA read alignment the closest precedent (LAST-TRAIN) is EM-based, not differentiable; no differentiable DNA read aligner was found.
expected_impact: Accuracy of indel placement in homopolymers; modest.
data_compute: NA19240 ONT reads aligned to NA19240 assemblies (truth); GPU helpful.
risks: Overfitting to one chemistry release; EM (LAST-TRAIN) may already capture most of the gain.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 ONT R10.4.1 reads aligned to its own HPRC r2 assemblies.
litmus_metric: Indel-placement concordance and homopolymer-length error against truth alignments.
litmus_baseline: minimap2 default scoring and LAST-TRAIN parameters; not measured.
litmus_target: >= 10% fewer homopolymer indel misplacements than LAST-TRAIN.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met on held-out chromosomes.
impact_justification: Small, chemistry-specific gains.
feasibility_justification: Needs custom training code.
novelty_justification: Not applied to DNA read alignment.

title: Fiber-seq reads as dual-use coverage and haplotype-informative chromatin signal
mechanism: Fiber-seq HiFi/ONT reads carry m6A footprints but are also accurate long reads; pool them as assembly coverage and test whether haplotype-specific chromatin (imprinted loci, X inactivation) adds phasing signal.
closest_prior_evidence: fibertools calls m6A and nucleosome footprints from single-molecule reads.
github: https://github.com/fiberseq/fibertools-rs (latest release v0.13.1; last push 2026-11; 74 stars)
status_evidence: HPRC r2 lists fiberseq_hifi for 21 samples and fiberseq_ont for 23; no assembler or phaser in the work reviewed uses m6A as a phasing feature.
expected_impact: Small coverage gain; niche phasing gain.
data_compute: HG01258 has HPRC r2 Fiber-seq HiFi.
risks: m6A labelling may slightly alter base accuracy; sparse phasing signal.
litmus_dataset: HG01258 HPRC r2 HiFi + Fiber-seq HiFi.
litmus_metric: Assembly QV and contiguity with and without Fiber-seq reads; phasing switch error.
litmus_target: No QV loss with added coverage; any phasing gain.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if QV is unchanged (+/-0.5) and contiguity improves.
impact_justification: Niche gain.
feasibility_justification: Few samples have Fiber-seq.
novelty_justification: Unexplored for assembly or phasing.

title: Compacted colored de Bruijn graphs for population-scale k-mer truth
mechanism: Build compacted, colored de Bruijn graphs (or SSHash/Fulgor dictionaries) over 1kG short-read k-mers of a trio or population to supply k-mer presence truth for assembly QC (hap-mers), novel-sequence discovery and contamination screening.
closest_prior_evidence: MetaGraph and Logan show petabase-scale k-mer indexing and assembly of public sequencing archives.
github: https://github.com/COMBINE-lab/cuttlefish (latest release v3.1.0; last push 2026-10; 101 stars) | https://github.com/algbio/ggcat (latest release v2.2.0; last push 2026-11; 101 stars) | https://github.com/jermp/sshash (latest release v6.0.0; last push 2026-11; 108 stars)
status_evidence: Released tools (Cuttlefish v3.1.0, GGCAT v2.2.0, SSHash v6.0.0) are widely used in metagenomics; human assembly QC still relies on Merqury/yak k-mer databases.
expected_impact: Memory-efficient multi-sample k-mer truth; modest gain over Merqury for single samples.
data_compute: Trio NYGC 30x CRAMs (~15 GB each); CPU; <= 64 GB RAM.
risks: Incremental over existing k-mer QC; error k-mers must be filtered.
litmus_dataset: NA19238/NA19239/NA19240 NYGC 30x CRAMs; NA19240 HPRC r2 assemblies.
litmus_metric: Hap-mer QV and switch error versus Merqury/yak; RAM and wall time.
litmus_target: QV identical within +/-0.5 at <= 50% of Merqury RAM.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met.
impact_justification: Incremental for single human samples.
feasibility_justification: Mature released tools.
novelty_justification: Implemented; new only as a QC application.

title: Locality-sensitive (fuzzy) seeds for noisy reads (SimHash, minmers)
mechanism: Hash groups of k-mers with SimHash so similar but non-identical seeds collide (BLEND), or sample minmers to estimate local Jaccard (MashMap3) for fast approximate mapping.
closest_prior_evidence: wfmash maps with MashMap 3.5 minmer sketches and aligns with WFA (README).
github: https://github.com/CMU-SAFARI/BLEND (latest release v.1.0.0; last push 2023-05; 47 stars) | https://github.com/marbl/MashMap (latest release v3.1.3; last push 2024-10; 292 stars) | https://github.com/waveygang/wfmash (latest release v0.24.2)
status_evidence: BLEND (a minimap2 fork) shows no activity since 2023-05; MashMap3 underpins wfmash, which produced the HPRC r2 impg PAFs.
expected_impact: Speed and sensitivity for noisy reads; modest for current accurate reads.
data_compute: NA19240 ONT R10 reads.
risks: More false seed hits; maintenance of forks.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 ONT R10.4.1 reads (chr20 region slice) and simulations from NA19240 haplotypes.
litmus_metric: Mapping accuracy on simulated truth; throughput.
litmus_target: >= 1.5x throughput at equal accuracy.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met.
impact_justification: Current reads are accurate enough for exact seeds.
feasibility_justification: Released fork; easy to benchmark.
novelty_justification: Implemented; MashMap3 is mainstream in wfmash.

title: Platform-aware alignment scoring and MAPQ for Element, Ultima and Roche SBX reads
mechanism: Short-read mappers use Illumina-tuned scores, while flow-based (Ultima) and avidity (Element) chemistries have distinct homopolymer and substitution profiles. Learn chemistry-specific scoring (LAST-TRAIN or differentiable DP) and recalibrate MAPQ per chemistry, evaluating against donor-specific assemblies.
closest_prior_evidence: A 2026 benchmark of nine chemistries on seven sequencers against donor-specific assemblies found the lowest substitution error rates for Element AVITI UltraQ and Roche SBX-D; Element reads with pangenome-aware DeepVariant were 23.6% more accurate than with existing methods.
github: https://github.com/Ultimagen/ugbio-utils (vendor utilities; 4 stars; last push 2026-11)
status_evidence: Vendor pipelines and caller models exist; the aligner releases reviewed expose no chemistry-specific presets for these platforms (aligner-level scoring remains open).
expected_impact: Accuracy of homopolymer indels; small for SNVs.
data_compute: 1kG-linked Element/Ultima/SBX runs were not located in this scan; donor-specific benchmarking currently uses HG002 (not a 1kG sample).
risks: Data availability for 1kG samples; fast chemistry turnover.
litmus_dataset: Flow-space and avidity error profiles simulated onto NA19240 HPRC r2 haplotypes until a 1kG-sample run is located.
litmus_metric: Homopolymer indel F1 and MAPQ calibration against truth.
litmus_target: >= 10% fewer homopolymer indel errors.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met on simulations and, when available, real 1kG-sample data.
impact_justification: Errors are small and mostly in homopolymers.
feasibility_justification: No 1kG-linked runs located.
novelty_justification: Aligner-level adaptation not found.

title: Learned indexes for seeding (BWA-MEME, Sapling, PLA-index)
mechanism: Replace suffix-array or hash lookups with learned models of the rank function (piecewise-linear or small neural models) that predict the position of a k-mer or suffix, corrected by a bounded local search.
closest_prior_evidence: BWA-MEME reports up to 3.45x seeding throughput over BWA-MEM2 with identical SAM output.
github: https://github.com/kaist-ina/BWA-MEME (latest release v1.0.6; last push 2026-06; 138 stars) | https://github.com/mkirsche/sapling (no tagged release)
status_evidence: BWA-MEME is released (v1.0.6) and active (push 2026-06), but default pipelines (bwa 0.7.19, bwa-mem2 v2.3) do not use learned indexes.
expected_impact: Speed of seeding only (outputs identical by design); memory may increase.
data_compute: Any 1kG CRAM region slice; arm64 portability of BWA-MEME not verified.
risks: Index memory; SIMD and x86 portability; seeding is rarely the end-to-end bottleneck.
litmus_dataset: NA19240 NYGC 30x CRAM, chr20 region slice.
litmus_metric: Seeding throughput, end-to-end wall time, peak RSS, byte-identical SAM.
litmus_target: >= 1.5x end-to-end speed-up at <= 64 GB RAM with identical SAM.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met on a declared host; fail if not portable or slower end to end.
impact_justification: Speed-only gain in a step that is rarely the bottleneck.
feasibility_justification: Released code, but memory and portability are uncertain.
novelty_justification: Implemented and published; only adoption is missing.

title: Streaming and adaptive-sampling alignment
mechanism: Map reads (or raw signal) as they are sequenced and eject off-target molecules (Read Until), or update targets dynamically with Bayesian experimental design.
closest_prior_evidence: BOSS-RUNS reduced low-coverage sites by 87.5% with 12.5% more SNPs detected in one reported example.
github: https://github.com/LooseLab/readfish (latest release v2026.1.0; last push 2026-10; 198 stars)
status_evidence: readfish v2026.1.0 is released.
expected_impact: Cost and targeted completeness; not a general aligner improvement.
data_compute: pod5 playback (HG00097 R10).
risks: True evaluation requires a live sequencer.
litmus_dataset: HG00097 R10 pod5 playback with an SD-gene target panel.
litmus_metric: On-target enrichment and decision latency.
litmus_target: Enrichment >= 3x at decision latency <= 1 s.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if met in playback.
impact_justification: Targeted use only.
feasibility_justification: Playback possible; live runs needed for full test.
novelty_justification: Mainstream.

title: Reinforcement learning for assembly path finding
mechanism: Formulate layout as a sequential decision process over an overlap graph and learn a policy (Q-learning or policy gradients) that extends contigs.
closest_prior_evidence: Published work analyses Q-learning assemblers on small genomes.
github: no repository found (GitHub search 'reinforcement learning genome assembly' returned 0)
status_evidence: Only toy-scale studies were found; no human-scale implementation.
expected_impact: Low near term; GNN and exact graph methods dominate.
data_compute: Small subgraphs from NA19240 assembly graphs.
risks: Sparse rewards and huge state spaces; no evidence of competitiveness at human scale.
litmus_dataset: SD-rich tangle subgraphs (<= 2 Mb) from the NA19240 hifiasm graph.
litmus_metric: Path accuracy against trio-phased NA19240 assemblies.
litmus_target: Match hifiasm path accuracy.
litmus_pass_fail: Pass if the RL path equals or beats hifiasm on >= 3 tangles; otherwise deprioritize.
impact_justification: No evidence of competitiveness beyond toy genomes.
feasibility_justification: Research-grade only; no human-scale code.
novelty_justification: Largely unexplored for human assembly.
